steps.title: Prepare Vero E6 cell suspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend Vero E6 cells in growth media to a concentration of 30,000 cells per 50 µL (6.0 × 10⁵ cells mL⁻¹), record the passage number, and transport the suspension from a clean tissue‑culture biosafety cabinet to the viral biosafety cabinet.

steps.title: Seed cells into 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Seed 50 µL of the cell suspension into each well of a white‑bottomed, tissue‑culture‑coated 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Add virus and incubate
steps.instruction: Dilute the virus of interest to an MOI = 0.01 in 50 µL per well; add this viral antigen to columns 2‑12 and add 50 µL blank media to column 1. Incubate the plate at 37 °C for 24 hours.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant and wash
steps.instruction: After incubation, aspirate the supernatant and wash the wells twice with PBS.

steps.title: Fix cells with paraformaldehyde
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 4 % paraformaldehyde to each well while in the biosafety cabinet, wrap the plate in plastic film, spray the exterior with 70 % ethanol, and transfer to a fume hood. Let fix for 20 minutes at room temperature, then discard the fixative into appropriate waste. Rinse wells three times with PBS, discard the rinse, and remove the plate from the fume hood.

steps.title: Permeabilize monolayer
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 0.5 % Triton X‑100 in PBS to each well and incubate at room temperature for 10–15 minutes. Rinse wells three times with PBS and discard the rinse.

steps.title: Block plate
steps.instruction: Add 100–200 µL of blocking agent to each well and place the plate at 4 °C overnight or for a minimum of 1 hour.

steps.title: Prepare serum dilution stock
steps.instruction: Thaw serum samples on ice, then dilute 10 µL heat‑inactivated serum into 990 µL diluent to create a 1 : 100 stock; store the stock for future repeats.

steps.title: Set up serial serum dilutions
steps.instruction: In an uncoated 96‑well assay plate, add 75 µL antibody‑dilution buffer to columns 2‑12. Add 150 µL of the 1 : 100 diluted serum to column 1 (final 1 : 100 starting dilution). Perform 1 : 2 serial dilutions by transferring 75 µL from one well to the next, changing tips each time.

steps.title: Add diluted sera to blocked plate
steps.instruction: Remove the blocking solution from the blocked plate, tap dry on blotting paper, and add 50 µL of each diluted serum sample to the corresponding wells (starting from the most dilute to the least; the same multichannel tip may be reused).

steps.title: Incubate sera with cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 4 hours or at 37 °C for 1 hour with gentle rocking.

steps.title: Wash after serum incubation
steps.instruction: Discard the serum solutions and rinse wells three times with PBS‑T, allowing each wash to sit for 3 minutes before removal to reduce background.

steps.title: Add secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of secondary antibody diluted in antibody‑dilution buffer to each well and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.

steps.title: Wash after secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Discard the secondary‑antibody solution and rinse wells three times with PBS‑T, letting each wash sit for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Dry plates
steps.instruction: Tap the plates dry on blotting paper and allow them to air‑dry for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add peroxidase substrate
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL peroxidase substrate to each well, then incubate at room temperature in the dark for 10 minutes or until signal development is sufficient.

steps.title: Determine endpoint titer
steps.instruction: Identify the last well in each column that shows visible foci; report the endpoint titer as the inverse of that dilution (1 : X).

steps.title: Store plate (optional)
steps.instruction: If the plate is to be stored, add 100 µL PBS to each well, wrap with plastic film or parafilm, and keep at 4 °C.
